### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

all of the above

### Question

I'm a new Neovim user who is also a mini user via kickstart!

From the mini help docs, I can see that calling setup on a module creates a global camel-cased Lua object. My question is whether there is a best practice for removing the undefined global warning that I believe Lua LSP is giving me on that object. (e.g. line 2 diagnostic below says `Undefined global 'MiniIcons'.`)

```lua
require('mini.icons').setup() 
MiniIcons.mock_nvim_web_devicons()
```

I'm installing mini with lazy (kickstart default) if that is relevant. Thank you in advance.

comment_data.body:
There are couple of ways to address this (none of which is "standard" per se):

- Create '.luarc.json' in the config root and tell it to address this specific diagnostic warning. Either by completely ignoring all such cases, ignoring specific variables, or downgrading the severity from a warning to a hint. The file's structure can be seen [here](https://luals.github.io/wiki/configuration/#luarcjson-file) with full schema [here](https://github.com/LuaLS/vscode-lua/blob/master/setting/schema.json).

    A more automated approach here would be to put cursor on the "undefined variable" and ask for code actions. In 'kickstart.nvim' it is done by [typing `gra`](https://github.com/nvim-lua/kickstart.nvim/blob/e79572c9e6978787af2bca164a85ab6821caeb7b/init.lua#L541). It will suggest ways to solve this issue.

    This is a relatively okay thing to do since [lua-language-server itself ignores some diagnostics](https://github.com/LuaLS/lua-language-server/blob/master/.luarc.json).

- Universally use `require('mini.xxx')` instead of `MiniXxx` global variable. These two deliver the same result. The first is in practice almost as fast as the second (`require()` caches its output), but more verbose.
- Ignore it. Which is what I do and, frankly, recommend.
